The MESH equations of every stage were solved together by Newton's method (Naphtali-Sandholm), started by the continuation in the relative volatilities (11 steps), in 4 iterations; every group of residuals is within its tolerance (state.residuals). Converged is not validated against data: the result is as good as the method and its parameters.

The vapour + liquid condenser (proposal 0026) at 326.2 K, fixed by vapour_distillate_kmol_h = 38.56: stage 1 is an equilibrium stage whose vapour leaves as the vapour distillate (outlet "vapour_distillate", 38.56 kmol/h) and whose liquid is split, with one composition, into the reflux and the liquid distillate (outlet "distillate", 4548.33 kmol/h). The reflux ratio is the reflux over the liquid distillate, 2 (over the whole distillate 1.98319); distillate_kmol_h is the whole distillate, liquid and vapour.

PR is the method here: Carbon dioxide is a light gas, which only an equation of state describes (gas-phase reactors and high-pressure loops are simulated so). For a liquid of the polar components alone (Methanol, Water) below about 10 bar, such as their distillation, an activity model (NRTL or UNIQUAC) would be more accurate (docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md).
